[LLM] NSO/Pegasus WhatsApp phishing redirector domains (ikhwancast/ghazacast/fr24cast) Delivery High
Detects any managed endpoint resolving or connecting to the three NSO-linked redirector domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) that Meta published as IOCs for the June 2026 WhatsApp 1-click spyware campaign. Hits should be treated as a direct attempted-Pegasus-delivery signal — the affected user is presumed to have been individually targeted (the campaign was tightly scoped to <10 users, primarily in Jordan/Lebanon). Rationale: Three Meta-published domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) are the only article-specific high-fidelity indicators. Cross-checked against Meta's own announcement, TechCrunch and The Hacker News reporting — all three sources name the same domains as the campaign IOCs. The campaign targeted <10 users primarily in Jordan/Lebanon, so even a single hit on a managed endpoint is presumed-targeted activity rather than noise. Cross-checked against: • https://about.fb.com/news/2026/06/fighting-spyware-an-update-from-whatsapp/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/meta-blocks-nso-groups-new-whatsapp.html • https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/08/whatsapp-says-it-caught-new-spyware-attacks-linked-to-nso-group-in-violation-of-court-order/ • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/08/nso-group-back-in-metas-crosshairs-after-alleged-whatsapp-targeting/5252105
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1071.001

    | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents", DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url=RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
let Clicks = UrlClickEvents

union Net, Clicks
| order by Timestamp desc
let NsoDomains = dynamic(["ikhwancast.com","ghazacast.com","fr24cast.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Detail=strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct, " action=", DeviceAction)),
(ImWebSession

(ImDnsActivity

  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Detail=strcat("qtype=", DnsQueryTypeName))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 8b5fee83-9f0b-4f8c-be7e-4d3a9c2a3f0a
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to the three NSO-linked redirector domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) published by Meta as IOCs for the June 2026 WhatsApp 1-click spyware campaign attributed to NSO Group / Pegasus.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hades Campaign: Graph ML PyPI Packages Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers, AI Analyst Misdirection, and a Wiper Deterrent

StepSecurity
2026-06-08 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On June 8, 2026, multiple Graph ML PyPI packages in the bioinformatics ecosystem were compromised in the Hades campaign, deploying cross-platform memory scrapers, AI prompt injections to misdirect scanners, and a token-revocation wiper.

ATT&CKT1027 T1059.001 T1190 T1195.002

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Hades Campaign PyPI install of compromised graph-ML / bio package versions · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The Hades Campaign: Graph ML PyPI Packages Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Hades Campaign python import hook spawning bun runtime from /tmp · [LLM] Hades Campaign persistence artifacts (systemd units + updater.py + lock/state files) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Hades Campaign GitHub commit-search C2 with firedalazer / DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom markers · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scrape of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Hades Campaign PyPI install of compromised graph-ML / bio package versions Delivery High
Detects pip/uv/poetry installation or on-disk arrival of the exact seven Hades Campaign package@version pairs (ensmallen 0.8.101, embiggen 0.11.97, gpsea 0.9.14, pyphetools 0.9.120, mflux-streamlit 0.0.3-0.0.4, nhmpy 2.4.7, ppkt2synergy 0.1.1). Catches the supply-chain compromise at the moment it lands on a developer or CI host, before the __init__.py import hook is ever triggered. Rationale: Pivots on the exact seven package@version pairs listed in the article's affected-versions table plus the .dist-info folder names pip writes to site-packages — every legitimate developer/CI install of these versions IS the compromise, so confidence is high. Dual surfaces (process exec AND file creation) catch out-of-band installs (uv lock, poetry, wheel cache copy).
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

let HadesDistInfo = dynamic(["ensmallen-0.8.101.dist-info","embiggen-0.11.97.dist-info","gpsea-0.9.14.dist-info","pyphetools-0.9.120.dist-info","mflux_streamlit-0.0.3.dist-info","mflux_streamlit-0.0.4.dist-info","nhmpy-2.4.7.dist-info","ppkt2synergy-0.1.1.dist-info"]);
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where FileName in~ ("pip","pip.exe","pip3","pip3.exe","uv","uv.exe","poetry","poetry.exe") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip.exe","pip3","pip3.exe")
 | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Surface="process", FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
 | where FolderPath has_any (HadesDistInfo) or FileName has_any (HadesPkgVersions)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Surface="file", FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="", FolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let HadesPkgVersions = dynamic(["ensmallen==0.8.101","ensmallen-0.8.101","embiggen==0.11.97","embiggen-0.11.97","gpsea==0.9.14","gpsea-0.9.14","pyphetools==0.9.120","pyphetools-0.9.120","mflux-streamlit==0.0.3","mflux-streamlit==0.0.4","mflux_streamlit-0.0.3","mflux_streamlit-0.0.4","nhmpy==2.4.7","nhmpy-2.4.7","ppkt2synergy==0.1.1","ppkt2synergy-0.1.1"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","uv","poetry") or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","uv","poetry")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions)

| regex("(ensmallen[-=]+0\.8\.101|embiggen[-=]+0\.11\.97|gpsea[-=]+0\.9\.14|pyphetools[-=]+0\.9\.120|mflux[-_]streamlit[-=]+0\.0\.[34]|nhmpy[-=]+2\.4\.7|ppkt2synergy[-=]+0\.1\.1)", field=CommandLine)

[LLM] Hades Campaign python import hook spawning bun runtime from /tmp Installation High
Detects the Hades Campaign __init__.py import-hook execution chain: a python interpreter spawning the Bun runtime out of /tmp/b/bun (or its zip extraction) running `_index.js`. This is the moment the malicious payload actually executes after package import, on Linux/macOS/Windows runners and developer hosts. Rationale: Bun is not a stock Linux/macOS/Windows binary and an out-of-tree path like `/tmp/b/bun` being launched by a python interpreter is the article's exact described chain (`_s.run([_b, "run", _j], ...)` in the deobfuscated import hook). Pairing parent=python with image=bun and a `/tmp/b/` or `_index.js` predicate is essentially the campaign signature with near-zero legitimate overlap.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.007 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "python"
| where (FileName =~ "bun" or FileName =~ "bun.exe")
      or FolderPath has_any (@"/tmp/b/", @"\Temp\b\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\b\")
      or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", @"\Temp\b\bun", "_index.js")
| extend BunPath = FolderPath, BunCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, BunPath, BunCmd,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "python" or ActingProcessName has "python"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
      or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", @"\Temp\b\bun", "_index.js")
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", "_index.js")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Campaign Bun Runtime Spawned by Python from /tmp
id: 2c6d8e1a-8b1e-4f4f-9d0c-1c1f1a2a3b02
description: Detects a python interpreter spawning the Bun JS runtime out of a /tmp/b/ (or %TEMP%\b\) staging directory while running _index.js — the Hades Campaign post-import payload execution.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/the-hades-campaign-pypi-packages
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains: 'python'
  child_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bun'
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '/tmp/b/bun'
      - '\Temp\b\bun'
  cmd_marker:
    CommandLine|contains: '_index.js'
  condition: parent and (child_image or child_path or cmd_marker)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*\/tmp\/b\/bun OR *\/bun) (@process.command_line:*_index.js* OR @process.command_line:*\/tmp\/b\/bun*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/python(3(\.\d+)?)?(\.exe)?$/i
| (ImageFileName=/[\\/]bun(\.exe)?$/i OR regex("([\\\\/]tmp[\\\\/]b[\\\\/]bun|[\\\\/]Temp[\\\\/]b[\\\\/]bun)", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("_index\.js", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","python3.11","python3.12","python3.13") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bun","bun.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*/tmp/b/bun","*\\Temp\\b\\bun.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*\\tmp\\b\\bun*","*/tmp/b/bun*","*_index.js*","*bun*run*_index.js*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","python3.11","python3.12","python3.13") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bun","bun.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*/tmp/b/bun","*\\Temp\\b\\bun.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*\\tmp\\b\\bun*","*/tmp/b/bun*","*_index.js*","*bun*run*_index.js*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Hades Campaign persistence artifacts (systemd units + updater.py + lock/state files) Installation High
Detects creation of the Hades Campaign on-disk persistence indicators: systemd user units update-monitor.service / gh-token-monitor.service, the C2 polling script updater.py under ~/.local/share/updater/, and the lock/state markers /tmp/.bun_ran, /tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock, /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. Any one of these on a non-detonation host is a high-fidelity indicator of active infection. Rationale: Every path here is verbatim from the article's IOC table or kill-chain block — `~/.local/share/updater/update.py`, `~/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service`, `~/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service`, `/tmp/.bun_ran`, `/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock`, `/var/tmp/.gh_update_state`. The chance of an unrelated legitimate process writing this exact combination of paths is essentially zero — the systemd-unit + lockfile pair alone is conclusive.
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let HadesFiles = dynamic(["update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state","tmp.0144018410.lock"]);
let HadesPaths = dynamic(["/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service","/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service","/.local/share/updater/update.py","/.local/share/updater/updater.py","/tmp/.bun_ran","/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName in (HadesFiles)
      or FolderPath has_any (HadesPaths)
      or (FolderPath has "/.local/share/updater" and FileName =~ "update.py")
      or (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName has_any ("update-monitor","gh-token-monitor"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileCreate","FileWrite","FileRename","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName in ("update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state","tmp.0144018410.lock","update.py","updater.py")
      or TargetFilePath has_any ("/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service","/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service","/.local/share/updater/","/tmp/.bun_ran","/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
| where not (TargetFileName =~ "update.py" and not(TargetFilePath has "/.local/share/updater"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Campaign Persistence Artifacts Written to Disk
id: 2c6d8e1a-8b1e-4f4f-9d0c-1c1f1a2a3b03
description: Detects creation of the Hades Campaign systemd user units, updater.py polling script, and lock/state files indicating active infection.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/the-hades-campaign-pypi-packages
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1543.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  by_full_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service'
      - '/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service'
      - '/.local/share/updater/update.py'
      - '/.local/share/updater/updater.py'
      - '/tmp/.bun_ran'
      - '/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock'
      - '/var/tmp/.gh_update_state'
  condition: by_full_path
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@file.path:(*\/\.config\/systemd\/user\/update-monitor.service OR *\/\.config\/systemd\/user\/gh-token-monitor.service OR *\/\.local\/share\/updater\/update*.py OR \/tmp\/.bun_ran OR \/tmp\/tmp.0144018410.lock OR \/var\/tmp\/.gh_update_state) OR @file.name:(update-monitor.service OR gh-token-monitor.service OR .bun_ran OR .gh_update_state OR tmp.0144018410.lock))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (regex("(/\\.config/systemd/user/(update-monitor|gh-token-monitor)\\.service|/\\.local/share/updater/update(r)?\\.py|/tmp/\\.bun_ran|/tmp/tmp\\.0144018410\\.lock|/var/tmp/\\.gh_update_state)", field=TargetFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service","*/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service","*/.local/share/updater/update.py","*/.local/share/updater/updater.py","/tmp/.bun_ran","/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state") OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service","tmp.0144018410.lock",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service","*/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service","*/.local/share/updater/update.py","*/.local/share/updater/updater.py","/tmp/.bun_ran","/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state") OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service","tmp.0144018410.lock",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Hades Campaign GitHub commit-search C2 with firedalazer / DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom markers Command & Control High
Detects the three independent GitHub-as-C2 channels used by the Hades Campaign: outbound traffic or process command lines referencing api.github.com/search/commits combined with the magic strings `firedalazer`, `DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, or `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`. These markers are the dead-drop discriminators the malware searches GitHub for to retrieve new payloads, token-revocation status, and exfil-destination repos. Rationale: The three magic strings (`firedalazer`, `DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`) are quoted verbatim in the kill-chain reconstruction as the attacker-controlled discriminators searched for via api.github.com/search/commits — they are unique enough that a single hit in URL or process command-line is high-confidence. Multi-surface (network + process) catches the malware whether the request leaves the host (network) or is logged by AMSI/script telemetry (process).
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web Endpoint.Processes
let HadesMarkers = dynamic(["firedalazer","DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesMarkers) or RemoteUrl has "search/commits"
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Surface="network", RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName),
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Surface="process", RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl="",
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine," | child=",ProcessCommandLine), InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let HadesMarkers = dynamic(["firedalazer","DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
 | where DestinationHostName has "api.github.com" or RequestURL has "api.github.com"
 | where RequestURL has_any (HadesMarkers) or Message has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor),
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
 | where Url has "api.github.com"
 | where Url has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, SourceUserName=SrcUsername, DestinationHostName=HttpHostName, RequestURL=Url, DeviceVendor=EventVendor),
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=DvcIpAddr, SourceUserName=ActorUsername, DestinationHostName="process", RequestURL=TargetProcessCommandLine, DeviceVendor=EventVendor)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Campaign GitHub C2 Magic Marker (firedalazer / DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom / TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime)
id: 2c6d8e1a-8b1e-4f4f-9d0c-1c1f1a2a3b04
description: Detects HTTP traffic to api.github.com containing one of the three Hades Campaign C2 magic markers, used to retrieve next-stage payloads and exfiltrate harvested credentials.
references:

author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1102.002
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1567.001
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  host:
    cs-host|contains: 'api.github.com'
  marker:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'firedalazer'
      - 'DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom'
      - 'TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime'
  condition: host and marker
level: high
(@http.url:*api.github.com* OR @url:*api.github.com*) (@http.url:(*firedalazer* OR *DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom* OR *TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*) OR @url:(*firedalazer* OR *DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom* OR *TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*firedalazer* OR *DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom* OR *TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/api\.github\.com$/i)
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2 | regex("(firedalazer|DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom|TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime)", field=CommandLine)}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId=TargetProcessId])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, CommandLine], function=count())

(`cim_Web_indexes` (url="*api.github.com/search/commits*" OR url="*api.github.com/repos*/commits*") (url="*firedalazer*" OR url="*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*" OR url="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR src_content="*firedalazer*" OR src_content="*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*" OR src_content="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*")) | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(url) as urls values(http_method) as methods by src user dest user_agent | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process IN ("*firedalazer*","*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*","*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
(`cim_Web_indexes` (url="*api.github.com/search/commits*" OR url="*api.github.com/repos*/commits*") (url="*firedalazer*" OR url="*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*" OR url="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR src_content="*firedalazer*" OR src_content="*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*" OR src_content="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*")) | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(url) as urls values(http_method) as methods by src user dest user_agent | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process IN ("*firedalazer*","*DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom*","*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
[LLM] Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scrape of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the article's tailored Linux/macOS/Windows memory-read primitives against the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process: a non-runner parent (python, pwsh, bun, mshta) referencing `Runner.Worker`, `/proc/<pid>/mem`, `task_for_pid`, `mach_vm_read_overwrite`, `ReadProcessMemory`, or `VirtualQueryEx` while a Runner.Worker process is co-resident on the host. Rationale: The article calls out the exact API surfaces per OS: `task_for_pid` + `mach_vm_read_overwrite` + `vm_region_basic_info_64` on macOS, `ReadProcessMemory`/`VirtualQueryEx`/`PROCESS_VM_READ` on Windows, and `/proc/<pid>/mem` + `/proc/<pid>/maps` on Linux — all targeting the `Runner.Worker` process specifically. Restricting to hosts where Runner.Worker actually exists kills FP from generic memory-debug tooling on non-CI machines, and limiting parents to python/pwsh/bun matches the Hades execution chain.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.001 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let MemPrimitives = dynamic(["Runner.Worker","task_for_pid","mach_vm_read_overwrite","vm_region_basic_info_64","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","PROCESS_VM_READ","/proc/","process_vm_readv"]);
let ScraperParents = dynamic(["python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","python3.11","python3.12","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh","bun","bun.exe"]);
let RunnerHosts =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "Runner.Worker" or FileName =~ "Runner.Worker.exe" or ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker"
    | distinct DeviceId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (RunnerHosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (ScraperParents) or FileName has_any (ScraperParents)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives)
| where not(FileName =~ "Runner.Worker" or FileName =~ "Runner.Worker.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let MemPrimitives = dynamic(["Runner.Worker","task_for_pid","mach_vm_read_overwrite","vm_region_basic_info_64","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","PROCESS_VM_READ","/proc/","process_vm_readv"]);
let ScraperParents = dynamic(["python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh","bun","bun.exe"]);
let RunnerHosts =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetProcessName has "Runner.Worker" or ActingProcessName has "Runner.Worker" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker"
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (RunnerHosts)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (ScraperParents) or ParentProcessName has_any (ScraperParents) or TargetProcessName has_any (ScraperParents)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives)
| where not(TargetProcessName has "Runner.Worker")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.command_line:(*Runner.Worker* OR *task_for_pid* OR *mach_vm_read* OR *ReadProcessMemory* OR *VirtualQueryEx* OR *\/proc\/*\/mem* OR *process_vm_readv*) OR @CommandLine:(*Runner.Worker* OR *ReadProcessMemory* OR *VirtualQueryEx*)) (@process.executable.path:(*\/python* OR *\/pwsh* OR *\/bun*) OR @Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\python3.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(python(3)?|pwsh|powershell|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(Runner\.Worker|task_for_pid|mach_vm_read|vm_region_basic_info|ReadProcessMemory|VirtualQueryEx|PROCESS_VM_READ|/proc/\\d+/mem|process_vm_readv)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT (ImageFileName=/Runner\.Worker(\.exe)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh","bun","bun.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*" OR Processes.process="*task_for_pid*" OR Processes.process="*mach_vm_read*" OR Processes.process="*ReadProcessMemory*" OR Processes.process="*VirtualQueryEx*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/*/mem*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/*/maps*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh","bun","bun.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*" OR Processes.process="*task_for_pid*" OR Processes.process="*mach_vm_read*" OR Processes.process="*ReadProcessMemory*" OR Processes.process="*VirtualQueryEx*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/*/mem*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/*/maps*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Check Point Remote Access VPN inbound auth from CVE-2026-50751 actor VPS IPs · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Qilin Linux ransomware ELF payload (CVE-2026-50751 campaign) — known MD5 file event · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Internal host outbound to CVE-2026-50751 Qilin actor IPs (post-bypass C2 / staging) · Network connections to article IPs / domains

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Rclone exfiltration from Check Point VPN gateway or post-bypass internal host · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Check Point Remote Access VPN inbound auth from CVE-2026-50751 actor VPS IPs Exploitation High
Detects inbound IKE/IPSec authentication or SSL VPN login attempts to Check Point Remote Access / Mobile Access gateways from the eight VPS IPs Check Point published as the CVE-2026-50751 / Qilin-affiliate infrastructure. Article-specific because it pivots on the published IOC IP set and on IKEv1 / Mobile Access ports. Rationale: Pivots on the eight VPS IPs Check Point published (article body) and the IKEv1 / Mobile Access ports the bypass requires. Cross-checked with Check Point's own blog and BleepingComputer write-up confirming the same IP set and hosting providers (Vultr, Shock Hosting, Kaupo Cloud HK). [LLM] Qilin Linux ransomware ELF payload (CVE-2026-50751 campaign) — known MD5 file event Installation High
Detects file write, file open, or process execution of a Linux ELF whose MD5 matches one of the two payloads Check Point attributed to the post-VPN-bypass Qilin affiliate stage. Specific to this article because it ships the two MD5 hashes the vendor published. Rationale: Both MD5s are taken verbatim from the article's IOC block and corroborated by Check Point's own advisory (linked to Qilin Linux ELF binaries per the BleepingComputer write-up). High-fidelity — file hashes do not collide with benign software in practice. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/

    | where MD5 in (qilinHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileEvent", ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
    | where MD5 in (qilinHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ProcessEvent", ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName)
| order by Timestamp asc

[LLM] Rclone exfiltration from Check Point VPN gateway or post-bypass internal host Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects rclone execution to a remote cloud target from a host that recently terminated a Remote Access VPN session — the exfiltration tradecraft Check Point and BleepingComputer attribute to this Qilin affiliate following CVE-2026-50751. Article-specific because it pairs rclone (named in the external advisories) with the Check Point campaign window. Rationale: Article body names rclone abuse and ELF download from actor-controlled infra in the post-exploit phase; cross-checked with Check Point's blog and BleepingComputer's write-up which both explicitly call out rclone. The combination of rclone binary + transfer verb + cloud remote prefix is the published tradecraft. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where FileName =~ "rclone" or FileName =~ "rclone.exe" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brclone\b"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("copy","sync","move","copyto","moveto","cat")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s(mega|s3|b2|drive|dropbox|onedrive|pcloud|box|gcs|azureblob|webdav|sftp|ftp|remote):"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)rclone(\.exe)?$" or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)rclone(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brclone\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("copy","sync","move","copyto","moveto","cat")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s(mega|s3|b2|drive|dropbox|onedrive|pcloud|box|gcs|azureblob|webdav|sftp|ftp|remote):"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
  selection_img:

      - '/rclone'

  selection_verb:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'copy'
      - 'sync'
      - 'move'
      - 'copyto'
      - 'moveto'
      - ' cat '
  selection_remote:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' mega:'

      - ' b2:'

      - ' dropbox:'
      - ' onedrive:'
      - ' pcloud:'
      - ' box:'
      - ' gcs:'
      - ' azureblob:'
      - ' webdav:'

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.security) (@process.name:(*rclone OR *rclone.exe OR *RCLONE.EXE) OR @Image:(*\\rclone.exe OR *\\Rclone.exe OR *\\RCLONE.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:(*/rclone OR */RCLONE)) (@process.command_line:(*copy* OR *sync* OR *move* OR *copyto* OR *moveto*) OR @CommandLine:(*copy* OR *sync* OR *move* OR *copyto* OR *moveto*)) (@process.command_line:(*mega:* OR *s3:* OR *b2:* OR *drive:* OR *dropbox:* OR *onedrive:* OR *pcloud:* OR *gcs:* OR *azureblob:*) OR @CommandLine:(*mega:* OR *s3:* OR *b2:* OR *drive:* OR *dropbox:* OR *onedrive:* OR *pcloud:* OR *gcs:* OR *azureblob:*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/(^|[\\/])rclone(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/\brclone\b/i)
| CommandLine=/\b(copy|sync|move|copyto|moveto|cat)\b/i
| CommandLine=/\s(mega|s3|b2|drive|dropbox|onedrive|pcloud|box|gcs|azureblob|webdav|sftp|ftp|remote):/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail   (detects the receiving side — anomalous PutObject bursts from outside-org credentials matching exfil shape)

| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["PutObject","CreateMultipartUpload","UploadPart","CompleteMultipartUpload"]
      and userAgent like /rclone/i
| stats count(*) as ops, count_distinct(requestParameters.bucketName) as buckets by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, userAgent, bin(5m)
| sort ops desc

[LLM] Internal host outbound to CVE-2026-50751 Qilin actor IPs (post-bypass C2 / staging) Command & Control High
Detects outbound network connections from any internal host to the eight VPS IPs Check Point published — i.e. an inside-out beacon or staging callback after the VPN gateway was compromised. Article-specific because the IPs are the exact post-exploit infrastructure named in the IOC block. Rationale: All eight IPs taken directly from the article IOC block; the BleepingComputer and Check Point sources confirm these are the actor-controlled VPS nodes used for both the bypass and post-exploit ELF staging. Outbound to a known-bad IP set is one of the cleanest signal shapes in detection engineering. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/08/attackers-had-month-long-head-start-on-patched-check-point-vpn-zero-day/5252438

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

DeviceEvents

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
