[LLM] Gogs Merge() argument injection — git rebase invoked with --exec= flag Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of the Gogs Merge() argument-injection zero-day (GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9, fixed in 0.14.3). The vulnerable code path passes a PR branch name beginning with -- directly to `git rebase`; supplying a branch named `--exec=<cmd>` causes git rebase to shell-exec the attacker command. This rule alerts whenever the gogs process spawns git with a rebase invocation that carries `--exec=` — there is no legitimate reason for the gogs daemon to ever run `git rebase --exec=`. Rationale: Anchored on the exact exploit primitive disclosed in the Rapid7 advisory and confirmed by Gogs PR #8301: an attacker-controlled branch name (`--exec=<cmd>`) reaches `git rebase` via Merge(). The cmdline pair `rebase` + `--exec=` under a `gogs` parent is uniquely diagnostic — the fixed code rejects leading-`-` branches and adds `--end-of-options`, so a patched server will not produce this pattern at all. Cross-checked: Rapid7 blog, BleepingComputer, Gogs PR #8301 / GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-authenticated-rce-via-argument-injection-gogs-unfixed/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301 • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/critical-gogs-rce-vulnerability-lets.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Gogs Merge() argument injection — GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9 / fixed in PR #8301
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("gogs","gogs.exe")
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("gogs","gogs.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("git","git.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rebase"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--exec="
     or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s--exec(=|\s)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Gogs Merge() argument injection — gogs spawns `git rebase --exec=`
let Window = 7d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
  | where ActingProcessName has "gogs" or ParentProcessName has "gogs"
  | where TargetProcessName has "git"
  | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "rebase" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--exec="
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
),

  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("gogs","gogs.exe")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\git.exe","/git")
  | where CommandLine has "rebase" and CommandLine has "--exec="
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName,
            ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName,
            TargetProcessName=NewProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=CommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Gogs daemon ancestry spawns shell / downloader (post-arg-injection RCE) Installation Medium
Defense-in-depth hunt for the post-exploitation stage of the Gogs Merge() argument-injection bug. After `git rebase --exec=<cmd>` runs, `<cmd>` is shell-exec'd as a descendant of the gogs daemon — so the diagnostic shape is gogs → git → (sh|bash|curl|wget|python|nc|powershell) with a payload-flavoured cmdline. Tuned to suppress legitimate Gogs server-side git hooks (pre-receive / post-receive / post-update). Rationale: Targets the second-order signal of the Gogs Merge() RCE: once `git rebase --exec=<cmd>` succeeds, `<cmd>` is shell-spawned with gogs as a near-ancestor. The downloader/reverse-shell regex (DownloadString, /dev/tcp/, bash -i, curl/wget, base64 -d) keeps signal high; the explicit exclusion of `hooks/(pre|post)-receive` paths removes the dominant legitimate noise source (gogs runs server-side git hooks as the gogs user). Cross-checked Rapid7 advisory plus PR #8301 patch which inserts `--end-of-options` confirming exec is the abuse target. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-authenticated-rce-via-argument-injection-gogs-unfixed/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301 • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

  "cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe",
  "curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe",
  "python","python3","perl","ruby","php",
  "nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat",
  "certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (GogsAncestor)
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (GogsAncestor)
| where FileName in~ (SuspiciousChildren)
// Discriminate from legit server-side git hooks (pre-receive / post-receive / post-update)
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(curl\s|wget\s|/dev/tcp/|bash\s+-i|nc\s+-[^\s]*[el]|chmod\s+\+x|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|certutil\s+-(urlcache|decode)|powershell\s+-(e|nop|w hidden)|IEX\s|DownloadString|base64\s+-d)"
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hooks/pre-receive","hooks/post-receive","hooks/update","hooks/post-update"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Internet-facing Gogs instances on pre-0.14.3 (CVE-pending Merge() injection) Reconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for Gogs servers running a version vulnerable to the Merge() argument-injection zero-day disclosed by Rapid7 — all releases up to and including 0.14.2 and any 0.15.0+dev build. Returns one row per device with vulnerable version, prioritised by whether the host is Internet-facing (Shadowserver tracks ~2,300 exposed Gogs servers globally; ~1,800 in Asia, ~300 in Europe). Rationale: Article explicitly names the vulnerable bracket — all releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev, fixed in 0.14.3. Confirmed via the Rapid7 vulnerability database entry and Gogs PR #8301. Joining DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing surfaces the assets that match Shadowserver's exposed-Gogs cohort (2,300 instances). This is a one-shot hunt to drive emergency patching, not a recurring alert. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/ • https://www.runzero.com/blog/gogs/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Internet-facing Gogs instances on vulnerable versions (≤ 0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev)
let GogsAssets = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where SoftwareName =~ "gogs" or (SoftwareVendor =~ "gogs" and SoftwareName has "gogs")
  | extend VerNoMeta = tostring(split(SoftwareVersion, "+")[0])
  | extend Parts = split(VerNoMeta, ".")
  | extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
  | extend IsDevBuild = SoftwareVersion has "+dev"
  | where Major == 0
        and ((Minor < 14)
          or (Minor == 14 and Patch <= 2)
          or (Minor == 15 and IsDevBuild));
GogsAssets
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing,
          SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
// Internet-facing Gogs instances on vulnerable versions — Sentinel (DeviceTvm* unified table)
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where SoftwareName =~ "gogs" or (SoftwareVendor =~ "gogs" and SoftwareName has "gogs")
| extend VerNoMeta = tostring(split(SoftwareVersion, "+")[0])
| extend Parts = split(VerNoMeta, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| extend IsDevBuild = SoftwareVersion has "+dev"
| where Major == 0
      and ((Minor < 14)
        or (Minor == 14 and Patch <= 2)
        or (Minor == 15 and IsDevBuild))
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing,
          SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| order by IsInternetFacing desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-39933", "CVE-2024-39932", "CVE-2026-26194", "CVE-2024-39930", "CVE-2025-8110", "CVE-2024-55947")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-39933", "CVE-2024-39932", "CVE-2026-26194", "CVE-2024-39930", "CVE-2025-8110", "CVE-2024-55947")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd") or SHA1 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd") or MD5 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd") or SHA1 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd") or MD5 in~ ("d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5", "c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6", "c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18", "f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348", "e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

Critical UniFi OS bug lets hackers gain root without authentication

BleepingComputer
2026-06-08 4 use cases 1 technique 5 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers can chain three already fixed vulnerabilities in the Ubiquiti UniFi OS server to execute remote code with root privileges and without authentication. [...]

CVEsCVE-2026-34908 CVE-2026-34909 CVE-2026-34910
ATT&CKT1190
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] UniFi OS CVE-2026-34908/34909 auth bypass via /api/auth/validate-sso/ URI normalization · [LLM] UniFi OS CVE-2026-34910 command injection via ucs/update/latest_package endpoint
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Anomalous child processes spawned under UniFi ucs-update service (post-exploitation)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] UniFi OS CVE-2026-34908/34909 auth bypass via /api/auth/validate-sso/ URI normalization Exploitation High
Hunts for unauthenticated requests to the UniFi OS Server that contain the auth-exempt prefix /api/auth/validate-sso/ but resolve (post-normalization) to protected backend routes. Bishop Fox confirmed this URI mismatch is the entry point of the unauth RCE chain on UniFi OS Server <= 5.0.6. Rationale: Anchors on the article's two named strings: the auth-exempt prefix '/api/auth/validate-sso/' and the protected target endpoint 'ucs/update/latest_package'. Combined with traversal / semicolon-based URI normalization artifacts (the documented root cause is a normalization mismatch between the auth filter and Nginx), the combination is high-fidelity. Cross-checked with the Bishop Fox advisory referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://bishopfox.com/blog/cve-2026-34908-34909-34910-ubiquiti-unifi-os-rce • https://community.ui.com/releases/UniFi-OS-Server-5-0-8/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// UniFi appliances typically aren't onboarded to MDE; this query catches Defender-protected Windows reverse proxies fronting UniFi.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 8443, 11443)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" or LocalIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("nginx.exe","haproxy.exe","caddy.exe","iisexpress.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where AdditionalFields has "/api/auth/validate-sso/"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("../","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e/","..%2f","ucs/update/latest_package",";","%3b")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Path A — Syslog from the UniFi appliance itself (nginx access log shipped via rsyslog)
let validate_sso_abuse = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("nginx","unifi-os","ucs")
| where SyslogMessage has "/api/auth/validate-sso/"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("../","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e/","..%2f","ucs/update/latest_package",";","%3b")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Path B — WAF / NGFW logs in CommonSecurityLog (DeviceName lives elsewhere; CSL uses DeviceVendor + DestinationHostName)
let validate_sso_csl = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort in (443, 8443, 11443)
| where RequestURL has "/api/auth/validate-sso/"
| where RequestURL has_any ("../","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e/","..%2f","ucs/update/latest_package",";","%3b")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication;
union validate_sso_abuse, validate_sso_csl
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: UniFi OS Auth Bypass via /api/auth/validate-sso/ URI Normalization Mismatch
id: 6c2f4d12-7b14-4a87-9f5c-c5b1c0ed3a1f
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-34908 / CVE-2026-34909 where the raw request URI begins with the auth-exempt /api/auth/validate-sso/ prefix but contains traversal / multi-route artifacts that normalize to a protected backend endpoint on UniFi OS Server <= 5.0.6.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-unifi-os-bug-lets-hackers-gain-root-without-authentication/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/api/auth/validate-sso/'
  traversal:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '../'
      - '%2e%2e%2f'
      - '%2e%2e/'
      - '..%2f'
      - 'ucs/update/latest_package'
      - ';'
      - '%3b'
  condition: selection and traversal
logsource:
  category: webserver
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:linux.syslog) (@http.url:*\/api\/auth\/validate-sso\/* OR @http.uri:*\/api\/auth\/validate-sso\/*) AND (@http.url:(*..\/* OR *%2e%2e%2f* OR *%2e%2e\/* OR *..%2f* OR *ucs\/update\/latest_package* OR *\;* OR *%3b*) OR @http.uri:(*..\/* OR *%2e%2e%2f* OR *%2e%2e\/* OR *..%2f* OR *ucs\/update\/latest_package* OR *\;* OR *%3b*))
// UniFi OS appliances rarely run the Falcon sensor; this catches sensor-protected reverse proxies in front of them.
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemotePort=/^(443|8443|11443)$/
| ContextImageFileName=/(nginx|haproxy|caddy)/i
| regex("/api/auth/validate-sso/", field=ContextBaseFileName) OR regex("/api/auth/validate-sso/", field=CommandLine)

[LLM] UniFi OS CVE-2026-34910 command injection via ucs/update/latest_package endpoint Exploitation High
Hunts for direct requests to the package-update endpoint 'ucs/update/latest_package' that carry shell-metacharacter payloads in the body or query string. Per Bishop Fox, this is the command-injection sink at the end of the chain — unvalidated user input is concatenated into a shell command executed by the ucs-update service account. Rationale: Direct lift of the two strings the article explicitly tells defenders to monitor ('ucs/update/latest_package' and the package-update injection sink), combined with the canonical Unix shell metacharacter set ( ; | ` $() && || newline & ) and their URL-encoded equivalents. Any legitimate UniFi update will not include shell metachars in the URI. Cross-checked Bishop Fox write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://bishopfox.com/blog/cve-2026-34908-34909-34910-ubiquiti-unifi-os-rce
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Catches Defender-protected reverse proxies (haproxy/nginx on Windows) sitting in front of UniFi appliances
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 8443, 11443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("nginx.exe","haproxy.exe","caddy.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where AdditionalFields has "ucs/update/latest_package"
| where AdditionalFields has_any (";","%3b","|","%7c","`","%60","$(","%24%28","%0a","%26","&&","||")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Path A — Syslog from the UniFi appliance (nginx/ucs application logs)
let ucs_update_injection_syslog = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("nginx","unifi-os","ucs","ucs-update")
| where SyslogMessage has "ucs/update/latest_package"
| where SyslogMessage has_any (";","%3b","|","%7c","`","%60","$(","%24%28","%0a","%26","&&","||")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Path B — Perimeter WAF / NGFW (CommonSecurityLog has no DeviceName, use DestinationHostName)
let ucs_update_injection_csl = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort in (443, 8443, 11443)
| where RequestURL has "ucs/update/latest_package"
| where RequestURL has_any (";","%3b","|","%7c","`","%60","$(","%24%28","%0a","%26")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL;
union ucs_update_injection_syslog, ucs_update_injection_csl
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: UniFi OS Command Injection on ucs/update/latest_package Endpoint (CVE-2026-34910)
id: ab19e7c2-2c14-4f4d-9120-1f9d6fb27c43
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-34910 where shell metacharacters are passed to the UniFi OS Server's /ucs/update/latest_package endpoint, enabling OS command execution under the ucs-update service account.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-unifi-os-bug-lets-hackers-gain-root-without-authentication/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: 'ucs/update/latest_package'
  metachars:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - ';'
      - '%3b'
      - '|'
      - '%7c'
      - '`'
      - '%60'
      - '$('
      - '%24%28'
      - '%0a'
      - '%26'
  condition: selection and metachars
logsource:
  category: webserver
level: critical
(source:nginx OR source:linux.syslog) (@http.url:*ucs\/update\/latest_package* OR @http.uri:*ucs\/update\/latest_package*) AND (@http.url:(*\;* OR *%3b* OR *\|* OR *%7c* OR *\`* OR *%60* OR *\$\(* OR *%24%28* OR *%0a* OR *%26*) OR @http.uri:(*\;* OR *%3b* OR *\|* OR *%7c* OR *\`* OR *%60* OR *\$\(* OR *%24%28* OR *%0a* OR *%26*))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemotePort=/^(443|8443|11443)$/
| ContextImageFileName=/(nginx|haproxy|caddy|ucs-update)/i
| regex("ucs/update/latest_package", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(;|%3b|\\||%7c|`|%60|\\$\\(|%24%28|%0a|%26|&&|\\|\\|)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.http_method) as method values(Web.status) as status from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest_port IN (443,8443,11443) Web.url="*ucs/update/latest_package*" (Web.url="*;*" OR Web.url="*%3b*" OR Web.url="*|*" OR Web.url="*%7c*" OR Web.url="*`*" OR Web.url="*%60*" OR Web.url="*$(*" OR Web.url="*%24%28*" OR Web.url="*%0a*" OR Web.url="*%26*") by Web.dest Web.src Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.http_method) as method values(Web.status) as status from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest_port IN (443,8443,11443) Web.url="*ucs/update/latest_package*" (Web.url="*;*" OR Web.url="*%3b*" OR Web.url="*|*" OR Web.url="*%7c*" OR Web.url="*`*" OR Web.url="*%60*" OR Web.url="*$(*" OR Web.url="*%24%28*" OR Web.url="*%0a*" OR Web.url="*%26*") by Web.dest Web.src Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Anomalous child processes spawned under UniFi ucs-update service (post-exploitation) Installation High
Hunts on UniFi OS appliances (Linux) for unexpected child processes of the ucs-update service binary — the post-injection foothold described by Bishop Fox. Legitimate ucs-update only invokes the package manager and a small set of UniFi helper binaries; spawn of bash/sh/curl/wget/nc/python is high-confidence post-exploitation. Rationale: Bishop Fox's recommended hunting hint is verbatim: 'suspicious child processes under ucs-update'. The ucs-update binary in normal operation only invokes the package manager and a couple of UniFi helper utilities — any interpreter, network tool, or sudo invocation downstream of it is post-exploitation. Also covers the sudo→root escalation step the article calls out. Cross-checked against: • https://bishopfox.com/blog/cve-2026-34908-34909-34910-ubiquiti-unifi-os-rce • https://community.ui.com/releases/UniFi-OS-Server-5-0-8/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1068 T1548.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Requires Defender for Endpoint on Linux on the UniFi appliance (or a Linux jump host running ucs-update tooling)
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ucs-update","ucs","unifi-os")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php","sudo","chmod","chown","base64","openssl","ssh","scp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// Path A — auditd/syslog from the appliance
let ucs_children_syslog = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("ucs-update","unifi-os")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/bash","/bin/sh","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/wget","/bin/nc","/usr/bin/socat","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/perl","sudo ","chmod ","base64 -d","openssl enc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Path B — ASIM process create (cross-vendor portable)
let ucs_children_asim = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("ucs-update","ucs","unifi-os")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php","sudo","chmod","chown","base64","openssl","ssh","scp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
union ucs_children_syslog, ucs_children_asim
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34908", "CVE-2026-34909", "CVE-2026-34910")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing has always been a numbers game. AI has turned it into a volume machine. Attackers can now create convincing emails, fake login pages, and tailored lures in minutes. Every polished message adds another case for Tier 1 to review, another link to inspect, and another alert that cannot be dismissed at a glance. As the queue grows, a credential theft attempt or malware delivery can easily

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:

            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'

            - 'downloadstring'

            - 'wget '

level: high

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ⚡ Weekly Recap: Instagram Account Hacks, Android Zero-Day, GitHub Worm and More
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'

level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
