Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:

level: high

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound IKEv1 traffic from Qilin VPN-bypass infrastructure to Check Point gateways
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Check Point IKEv1 Remote Access VPN session with no machine certificate (CVE-2026-50751 bypass shape)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Qilin post-compromise payload hashes (52fda5c1, 51d39aa3) on hosts reachable from VPN concentrator · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Long-lived VPN tunnel from VPS hosting ranges (Vultr/Cogent) attributed to Qilin VPN-bypass C2 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Inbound IKEv1 traffic from Qilin VPN-bypass infrastructure to Check Point gateways Delivery High
Hunts for inbound IKE/IPsec traffic (UDP/500, UDP/4500, ESP) sourced from the eight IP addresses attributed to the CVE-2026-50751 exploitation campaign against Check Point Remote Access / Mobile Access / Spark / Security Gateway products. Any successful association from these IPs against a Check Point firewall is a high-confidence indicator of the Qilin-affiliated VPN auth bypass. Rationale: Uses the eight attacker IPs from Phase 1/3 of the kill-chain (article-confirmed). Pairs them with IKE/IPsec ports (UDP 500/4500/ESP) so the detection fires only on VPN-shape traffic, not generic web noise. Cross-checked against: • https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk183303
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167")
| where RemotePort in (500, 4500) or Protocol =~ "esp"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let QilinIPs = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor has "Check Point"
| where SourceIP in (QilinIPs)
| where DestinationPort in (500, 4500) or ApplicationProtocol in~ ("ike","isakmp","esp","ipsec")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Activity, DeviceAction, SourceIP, SourcePort, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, ApplicationProtocol, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Check Point IKEv1 Remote Access VPN session with no machine certificate (CVE-2026-50751 bypass shape) Exploitation High
Hunts for successful Remote Access / Mobile Access VPN authentications that negotiated over IKEv1 without a machine certificate — the exact configuration the CVE-2026-50751 auth bypass targets. Surfaces gateways still accepting legacy RA clients that need to be hardened, and any session that successfully authenticated via the vulnerable path during the May 7 onwards exploitation window. Rationale: Targets the exact misconfiguration the article calls out: IKEv1 + legacy RA client + no mandatory machine certificate. Fires on the vulnerable shape regardless of source IP, so it catches exploitation from IPs not yet on the IOC list. Cross-checked Check Point advisory sk183303 wording. Cross-checked against: • https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk183303 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/
ATT&CKT1190 T1556 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// Downstream view — endpoints authenticating to AD via Check Point VPN pool, no Defender direct visibility of the IKE handshake itself
let VpnAttackerSrc = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);
IdentityLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where Protocol in~ ("Kerberos","NTLM","Ldap")
| where IPAddress in (VpnAttackerSrc)
   or DeviceName has_any ("vpn","ra-","mobileaccess","checkpoint")
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountUpn, AccountName, IPAddress, DeviceName, Protocol, LogonType, Application
| order by Timestamp desc
let QilinIPs = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where DeviceVendor has "Check Point"
| where Activity has_any ("Log In","Authentication","VPN Successful","Key Install","IKE")
| where DeviceCustomString1 has "IKEv1" or DeviceCustomString2 has "IKEv1" or Message has "IKEv1" or AdditionalExtensions has "IKEv1"
| where not(Message has_any ("machine_certificate","machine certificate","cert_auth")) and not(AdditionalExtensions has_any ("machine_certificate","machine certificate"))
| extend HitsAttackerIP = iff(SourceIP in (QilinIPs), "YES", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Activity, DeviceAction, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, ApplicationProtocol, HitsAttackerIP, Message
| order by HitsAttackerIP desc, TimeGenerated desc
source:checkpoint (@evt.name:("Log In" OR Authentication OR "VPN Successful" OR "Key Install")) AND (@ike.version:1 OR @message:IKEv1) AND -@auth.method:(machine_certificate OR cert)

[LLM] Long-lived VPN tunnel from VPS hosting ranges (Vultr/Cogent) attributed to Qilin VPN-bypass C2 Command & Control Medium
Hunts for inbound VPN sessions that stay open for hours from the eight Qilin-attributed IPs, plus any east-west traffic from the VPN-pool address those sessions were assigned. Models the article's described C2 pattern: attacker holds an interactive remote-access tunnel for hands-on-keyboard activity, traffic appears to originate from a trusted RA-VPN IP. Rationale: Pivots on the Phase 3 C2 hint that several attacker IPs sit in Vultr / Cogent VPS ranges and the tunnels are long-lived for hands-on-keyboard activity. Combines IP IOCs with a duration threshold so a one-off probe is filtered out — only sustained sessions surface. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1572

| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff("minute", LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where DurationMin >= 30 or Connections >= 50

| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff("minute", LastSeen, FirstSeen)

[LLM] Qilin post-compromise payload hashes (52fda5c1, 51d39aa3) on hosts reachable from VPN concentrator Installation High
Alerts on execution, file write, or image load of the two MD5 hashes attributed to the post-exploitation activity of the Qilin ransomware affiliate after CVE-2026-50751 was exploited. Highest-fidelity signal in the chain — anywhere these hashes appear on an internal host is a confirmed Qilin landing. Rationale: Both hashes are Phase 2/4 IOCs attributed to the confirmed Qilin post-compromise activity in the article and the kill-chain block. Hash hits are deterministic — no rephrasing needed; any match anywhere on the estate is high-severity. Sentinel union covers ASIM, SecurityEvent 4688 and CommonSecurityLog so detection works whether the customer uses MDE, Sysmon, or a third-party EDR shipping to CEF. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1032/
ATT&CKT1486 T1657 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let QilinHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689","51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
   | where MD5 in (QilinHashes) or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (QilinHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, EventTable="DeviceProcessEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
   | where MD5 in (QilinHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, EventTable="DeviceFileEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine="", AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
   | where MD5 in (QilinHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, EventTable="DeviceImageLoadEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine="", AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="")
| order by Timestamp desc
let QilinHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689","51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where MD5 in (QilinHashes) or Hash in (QilinHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, EventTable="ImProcessCreate", Host=DvcHostname, ActorUsername, FileName=ActingProcessName, FilePath="", MD5, SHA256, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ParentCommandLine=ParentProcessCommandLine),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where TargetFileMD5 in (QilinHashes) or Hash in (QilinHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, EventTable="ImFileEvent", Host=DvcHostname, ActorUsername, FileName=TargetFileName, FilePath=TargetFilePath, MD5=TargetFileMD5, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentImage=ActingProcessName, ParentCommandLine=""),
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where EventID == 4688
   | where FileHash has_any (QilinHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, EventTable="SecurityEvent4688", Host=Computer, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName, FileName=NewProcessName, FilePath=NewProcessName, MD5=FileHash, SHA256="", CommandLine, ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ParentCommandLine=""),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where FileHash in~ (QilinHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, EventTable="CommonSecurityLog", Host=coalesce(SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DeviceName), ActorUsername=SourceUserName, FileName, FilePath, MD5=FileHash, SHA256="", CommandLine="", ParentImage=ProcessName, ParentCommandLine="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Qilin / Agenda affiliate payload hashes following CVE-2026-50751 exploitation

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VerdantBamboo Deploys BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances

The Hacker News
2026-06-08 14 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A China-nexus cyber espionage group has been observed deploying a BSD variant of a known backdoor called BRICKSTORM, as well as two other malware families codenamed PLENET (aka GRIMBOLT) and AGENTPSD to target Linux systems. The activity has been attributed by Volexity to a threat cluster it tracks as VerdantBamboo, which it said overlaps with hacking groups known as Clay Typhoon (Microsoft),

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] M365 / Entra sign-ins sourced from BRICKSTORM C2 IP 149.248.11.71 Command & Control High
Hunts Microsoft 365 / Entra ID sign-in events whose source IP matches the VerdantBamboo C2 address published by Volexity. Because the actor proxied through compromised Egnyte Storage Sync + pfSense BRICKSTORM SOCKS relays to blend into Conditional Access policies, any direct sign-in from this IP indicates either a misconfigured tunnel or direct actor probing. Rationale: 149.248.11.71 is the sole IP IOC published by Volexity and reposted by Bleeping Computer / Cybersecuritynews — high-fidelity point IOC. Cross-checked Volexity report and Mallory.ai write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-apt-deploys-new-malware-to-keep-access-to-hacked-networks/ • https://www.mallory.ai/stories/019e9476-afd4-71fe-a6f0-7dff94b7f250

[LLM] VerdantBamboo BRICKSTORM / PLENET / AGENTPSD file-hash IOCs Installation High
Point-detection on the eight SHA256, four SHA1 and four MD5 hashes Volexity published for the BSD BRICKSTORM variant, PLENET (.NET AOT) and AGENTPSD (Python reverse shell). Matches across DeviceFileEvents and DeviceProcessEvents so we catch both landing and execution attempts on any Defender-for-Linux / Windows host. Rationale: All 16 hashes published in Volexity's June 2026 Verdant Bamboo blog; cross-checked against the BleepingComputer reposting of the IOC list. Hash detections have negligible FP rate; the broader IOC pivot covers the three malware families (BRICKSTORM BSD, PLENET, AGENTPSD) listed in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-apt-deploys-new-malware-to-keep-access-to-hacked-networks/ • https://github.com/mandiant/brickstorm-scanner

[LLM] AGENTPSD-style Python reverse shell spawned by sshd on Linux / NAS Installation Medium
Hunts the AGENTPSD deployment pattern Volexity describes: VerdantBamboo SSHed into Synology NAS / Linux appliances and dropped a Python-based reverse shell. Surfaces python3 / python processes whose parent is sshd and which subsequently open an outbound socket — a behaviour pattern that survives even when the static hashes mutate. Rationale: The article specifically calls out AGENTPSD as a Python reverse shell deployed over SSH to the Synology NAS. Parent=sshd + child=python is a tight behavioural pair on appliances where Python is rarely launched interactively; the cmd-line tokens are the canonical Python reverse-shell idioms. Cross-checked Volexity blog for the deployment vector (SSH). Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/chinese-apt-verdantbamboo-uses-brickstorm-malware/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1021.004 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName == "sshd"
| where FileName in~ ("python","python2","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("socket.", "subprocess.", "pty.spawn", "os.dup2", "-c import", "connect((", "/bin/sh", "/bin/bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "sshd"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/python(2|3)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("socket.", "subprocess.", "pty.spawn", "os.dup2", "-c import", "connect((", "/bin/sh", "/bin/bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

description: Detects a python interpreter spawned directly by sshd on a Linux / BSD host with command-line arguments matching reverse-shell semantics (socket import, pty.spawn, os.dup2, connect to /bin/sh). Maps to the VerdantBamboo AGENTPSD deployment pattern Volexity documented (June 2026).

[LLM] Outbound endpoint connections to BRICKSTORM C2 IP 149.248.11.71 Command & Control High
Catches any endpoint, server or appliance making an outbound network connection to the VerdantBamboo BRICKSTORM C2 address. Distinct pivot from UC1 (M365 sign-ins) — this targets the BRICKSTORM SOCKS callback channel rather than the resulting Entra session, so it fires even if the proxy never reaches a successful sign-in. Rationale: 149.248.11.71 is the only network-layer IOC Volexity published. The detection covers every host that BRICKSTORM might call out from (Storage Sync, pfSense, Synology NAS, Windows endpoints) by hitting both EDR and firewall telemetry. Cross-checked Volexity, BleepingComputer and Mallory.ai. Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-apt-deploys-new-malware-to-keep-access-to-hacked-networks/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "149.248.11.71"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "149.248.11.71"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcAction, SrcUsername),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP == "149.248.11.71"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceAction, SourceUserName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] pfSense / firewall config change enabling Web SSL VPN after admin login Installation Medium
Hunts the VerdantBamboo re-entry tactic Volexity documents — after stolen admin credentials let them into the firewall, the actor enabled web SSL VPN access to the appliance and used it for ongoing entry. Surfaces config-write events on the firewall WebGUI / SSL VPN service originating from previously-unseen admin source IPs, correlated to a successful admin login in the preceding 15 minutes. Rationale: Volexity explicitly describes the actor reconnecting to the firewall with stolen admin credentials and then enabling web SSL VPN access on the device — Syslog/php-fpm/configd messages on pfSense are the canonical witness for that change. Defender / Falcon are left empty because pfSense appliances are not typically EDR-instrumented; Sigma is left empty because the correlation requires a time-window join between two log events (rule explicitly forbidden for single-event-shape Sigma). Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://cyberpress.org/verdantbamboo-breaches-pfsense-firewall/
ATT&CKT1556 T1133 T1078
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let AdminLogins = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv") or ProcessName in ("sshd","webConfigurator","php-fpm")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("Successful login for user 'admin'", "Successful webConfigurator login", "Accepted password for admin")
    | extend AdminIP = extract(@"from ([\d\.]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | project AdminLoginTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, AdminIP;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ProcessName in ("php-fpm","configd","check_reload_status","openvpn")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("openvpn-server", "server1.conf", "webgui:", "system_advanced_admin", "WebGUI enabled", "User-Manager: 'admin'")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("add","enable","modify","saved")
| join kind=inner AdminLogins on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (AdminLoginTime .. AdminLoginTime + 15m)
| project AdminLoginTime, ConfigChangeTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, AdminIP, SyslogMessage
| order by ConfigChangeTime desc
source:linux.syslog @host.name:*pfsense* @process.name:(php-fpm OR configd OR check_reload_status OR openvpn) ("openvpn-server" OR "server1.conf" OR "WebGUI enabled" OR "system_advanced_admin" OR "User-Manager: 'admin'")

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

DeviceProcessEvents

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Critical

UNC3753 Used Vishing and Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign

The Hacker News
2026-06-08 18 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a financially motivated data theft extortion campaign that has targeted dozens of organizations across professional, legal, and financial services in the U.S. between January and May 2026. The activity has been attributed by Google Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) to a threat actor dubbed UNC3753, which is also known as

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Quick Assist launched followed by remote interactive session (UNC3753 vishing pretext) · [LLM] Privnote[.]com self-destructing-note URL access from corporate endpoint · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AnyDesk, Bomgar, SuperOps or Zoho Assist installer execution (UNC3753 RMM foothold) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to UNC3753 (Luna Moth) infrastructure IPs · [LLM] Outbound mail to or domain lookup of business-data-leaks[.]com (UNC3753 extortion infrastructure) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] WinSCP or Rclone exfiltration from end-user workstations · [LLM] USB mass-storage attached followed by bulk file copy (UNC3753 physical intrusion) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Quick Assist launched followed by remote interactive session (UNC3753 vishing pretext) Delivery Medium
Detects users launching Microsoft Quick Assist (quickassist.exe) and then a remote-controlled session beginning shortly after — the UNC3753 pretext for IT-help-desk vishing. Article-specific because UNC3753 explicitly named Quick Assist alongside Zoom/Teams as the screen-share entry vector. Rationale: Article names Quick Assist explicitly as a vector. The binary is fairly rare in most enterprises (Teams/Zoom are more common), so plain execution is a hunt-grade pivot. Corroborated with CISA & Microsoft advisories on Storm-1811/Quick Assist abuse. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1566.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "quickassist.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "quickassist.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\quickassist.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\quickassist.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Quick Assist Execution (UNC3753 Vishing Pretext)
id: 6f2a8b3c-1c7d-4f50-a47b-2a3df9b1a401
description: Detects launch of Microsoft Quick Assist (quickassist.exe), abused by UNC3753/Luna Moth/SRG to obtain remote-control screen-share sessions after vishing IT-helpdesk pretexts.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unc3753-used-vishing-and-physical.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1566.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\quickassist.exe'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\quickassist.exe OR *\QuickAssist.exe OR *\QUICKASSIST.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\quickassist\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="quickassist.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="quickassist.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="quickassist.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="quickassist.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
[LLM] AnyDesk, Bomgar, SuperOps or Zoho Assist installer execution (UNC3753 RMM foothold) Installation Medium
Detects fresh installation or first-time execution of the specific RMM tools UNC3753 instructs vishing victims to install (AnyDesk, Bomgar, SuperOps RMM, Zoho Assist). High-value hunting pivot since the article names these four explicitly. Rationale: Article explicitly names these four RMM tools as the post-vishing foothold mechanism. None should be ubiquitous in an org with a single sanctioned RMM — flag the deviations. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-156a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1020/
ATT&CKT1219 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let RMMBinaries = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","bomgar-scc.exe","bomgarportal.exe","bomgar.exe","superops.rmm.agent.exe","superops_agent.exe","zohoassist.exe","zohomeeting.exe","za_connect.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ (RMMBinaries)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AnyDesk","Bomgar","SuperOps","Zoho Assist")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let RMMBinaries = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","bomgar-scc.exe","bomgarportal.exe","bomgar.exe","superops.rmm.agent.exe","superops_agent.exe","zohoassist.exe","zohomeeting.exe","za_connect.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcessFile = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcessFile in (RMMBinaries)
   or CommandLine has_any ("AnyDesk","Bomgar","SuperOps","Zoho Assist")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Privnote[.]com self-destructing-note URL access from corporate endpoint Delivery Medium
Detects users browsing to privnote.com — the legitimate self-destruct-note service UNC3753 uses to deliver RMM install instructions during vishing calls without leaving recoverable evidence. Article-specific: privnote was explicitly named as the delivery channel. Rationale: Privnote is a legitimate but rarely-business-justified service. Article calls it out as UNC3753's instruction-delivery mechanism — DNS / proxy visibility on it is a cheap, high-signal pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://krebsonsecurity.com/2023/05/phishing-domains-tanked-after-meta-sued-freenom/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/
ATT&CKT1102 T1566.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Resolution.DNS
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "privnote.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","mssense.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DnsQuery has "privnote.com"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outbound connection to UNC3753 (Luna Moth) infrastructure IPs Command & Control High
Detects any endpoint or network egress to the seven IPs Mandiant/GTIG tied to UNC3753 (192.236.147.131, 192.236.147.138, 193.141.60.212, 192.236.154.158, 192.236.146.173, 174.169.162.62, 64.94.84.97). High-confidence alerting tier since these are specific IOCs. Rationale: Seven specific IOCs from the article — second-source corroborated against Mandiant/GTIG attribution to UNC3753 and FBI advisory. Direct-IP detections are high fidelity and low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1020/ • https://www.ic3.gov/Media/News/2024/240712.pdf
ATT&CKT1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Network
let UNC3753_IPs = dynamic(["192.236.147.131","192.236.147.138","193.141.60.212","192.236.154.158","192.236.146.173","174.169.162.62","64.94.84.97"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (UNC3753_IPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let UNC3753_IPs = dynamic(["192.236.147.131","192.236.147.138","193.141.60.212","192.236.154.158","192.236.146.173","174.169.162.62","64.94.84.97"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (UNC3753_IPs)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, EventVendor, EventProduct, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WinSCP or Rclone exfiltration from end-user workstations Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects WinSCP and Rclone process execution from user-context endpoints — UNC3753's named exfiltration tooling for staged sensitive data. Filters out IT-admin and backup-team baseline use. Rationale: Article names WinSCP and Rclone as the staged-exfil tooling. Both binaries are extremely rare in finance/legal services user contexts. Strong hunt-grade signal when scoped away from backup/IT. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1040/ • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-061a
ATT&CKT1567 T1048
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("winscp.exe","winscp.com","rclone.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rclone copy","rclone sync","rclone copyto","winscp.com /command","open sftp://","open ftps://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("backupsvc","sftpsvc"))
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("backup","jumpbox","bastion"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcessFile = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcessFile in ("winscp.exe","winscp.com","rclone.exe")
   or CommandLine has_any ("rclone copy","rclone sync","rclone copyto","winscp.com /command","open sftp://","open ftps://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (SubjectUserName has_any ("backupsvc","sftpsvc"))
| where not (Computer has_any ("backup","jumpbox","bastion"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] USB mass-storage attached followed by bulk file copy (UNC3753 physical intrusion) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects USB mass-storage attach events followed within 30 minutes by a high volume of file writes/reads against the device — modelling the FBI-reported UNC3753 escalation where threat actors enter offices in person posing as IT technicians and exfiltrate via external USB drives. Rationale: FBI advisory and the article both call out the new in-person USB-exfil escalation. Removable-media + bulk-write correlation on the user's workstation is the only telemetry surface for this physical-intrusion variant. Image [1] (vishing.jpg) reinforces the broader social-engineering pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ic3.gov/Media/News/2024/240712.pdf • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1052/001/
ATT&CKT1052.001 T1200
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let USBAttach = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("UsbDriveMounted","PnpDeviceConnected","UsbDriveDriveLetterChanged")
    | project AttachTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, AdditionalFields;
let BulkCopy = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
    | summarize FileCount = count(), FirstWrite=min(Timestamp), LastWrite=max(Timestamp), SampleFile=any(FolderPath) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
    | where FileCount > 50;
USBAttach
| join kind=inner BulkCopy on DeviceId
| where FirstWrite between (AttachTime .. AttachTime + 30m)
| project AttachTime, FirstWrite, LastWrite, DeviceName, AccountName, FileCount, SampleFile, AdditionalFields
| order by AttachTime desc
let USBAttach = Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventLog == "Microsoft-Windows-DriverFrameworks-UserMode/Operational"
       or (EventLog == "System" and EventID in (20001,20003))
    | project AttachTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID;
let BulkCopy = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4663
    | where ObjectName matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
    | summarize FileCount = count(), FirstAccess=min(TimeGenerated), LastAccess=max(TimeGenerated), SampleFile=any(ObjectName) by Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName
    | where FileCount > 50;
USBAttach
| join kind=inner BulkCopy on Computer
| where FirstAccess between (AttachTime .. AttachTime + 30m)
| project AttachTime, FirstAccess, LastAccess, Computer, AccountName, FileCount, SampleFile
| order by AttachTime desc
source:windows.security @EventID:6416 @ClassName:DiskDrive
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^[D-Z]:\\\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count(as=FileCount))
| FileCount > 50
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.file_path IN ("E:\\*","F:\\*","G:\\*","H:\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 50 AND firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.file_path IN ("E:\\*","F:\\*","G:\\*","H:\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 50 AND firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
[LLM] Outbound mail to or domain lookup of business-data-leaks[.]com (UNC3753 extortion infrastructure) Command & Control High
Detects communications with business-data-leaks.com — the UNC3753 / Luna Moth data-leak-site domain referenced in extortion follow-ups. Any DNS lookup or email contact with this domain from the enterprise indicates either an in-progress extortion or a curious researcher. Rationale: Domain explicitly referenced in the article (LEAKEDDATA leak site) and corroborated by Mandiant attribution. Hits should be near-zero in normal enterprise traffic. Image [2] (LEAKEDDATA.png) corroborates the leak-site branding. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1020/ • https://www.ic3.gov/Media/News/2024/240712.pdf
ATT&CKT1567 T1657
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Email.All_Email
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where RemoteUrl has "business-data-leaks.com" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents", InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
(EmailEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SenderFromAddress has "business-data-leaks.com" or SenderMailFromDomain has "business-data-leaks.com" | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", Source="EmailEvents", InitiatingProcessAccountName=RecipientEmailAddress, InitiatingProcessFileName=Subject, RemoteUrl=SenderFromAddress, RemoteIP="")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has "business-data-leaks.com" | project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery),
(OfficeActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Operation has_any ("Send","MailItemsAccessed") | where tostring(EventData) has "business-data-leaks.com" | project TimeGenerated, Source="Office365", SrcHostname="", SrcIpAddr=ClientIP, SrcUsername=UserId, Indicator="business-data-leaks.com")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
