Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"

          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

DeviceEvents

—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-42271 — BerriAI LiteLLM Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C0XMO botnet C2 beacon to hardcoded Fortinet-attributed IPs Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connections from internal hosts (Linux servers, IoT-adjacent infra, or any endpoint behind perimeter firewalls) to the three IPs Fortinet ties to C0XMO operators. Includes the German-hosted source/scan IP and the two additional C2/relay IPs. Rationale: Three named C2/scan IPs (217.160.125.125, 176.100.37.91, 85.215.131.70) are concrete, low-FP atomic indicators. Schema-aware union over CommonSecurityLog and ImNetworkSession to catch both raw NGFW shippers and ASIM-normalised feeds without referencing the missing `DeviceName`/`Protocol` columns.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let C2IPs = dynamic(["217.160.125.125","176.100.37.91","85.215.131.70"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2IPs = dynamic(["217.160.125.125","176.100.37.91","85.215.131.70"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (C2IPs) or SourceIP in (C2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, Product=DeviceProduct, SrcHost=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, DstIp=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort, AppProto=ApplicationProtocol, DeviceAction
),
(
    ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (C2IPs) or SrcIpAddr in (C2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, Product=EventProduct, SrcHost=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, DstIp=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, AppProto=NetworkApplicationProtocol, NetworkProto=NetworkProtocol, Action=DvcAction
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C0XMO Gafgyt persistence binary drop to hidden /tmp/.sys paths Installation High
Hunts creation of files at the exact hidden paths Fortinet documented C0XMO copies itself into on a freshly compromised Linux/IoT host: /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys. These dot-prefixed names in world-writable tmpfs locations are not used by mainstream Linux software. Rationale: Fortinet quotes those three exact paths verbatim — `/tmp/.sys`, `/var/tmp/.sys`, `/dev/shm/.sys`. Dot-prefix + tmpfs is not a path any mainstream distro package, container runtime, or admin tool writes to, so atomic-path match is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1564.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ ("/tmp/.sys","/var/tmp/.sys","/dev/shm/.sys")
   or (FileName == ".sys" and FolderPath in~ ("/tmp","/var/tmp","/dev/shm"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/tmp/.sys","/var/tmp/.sys","/dev/shm/.sys")
   or (TargetFileName == ".sys" and TargetFilePath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C0XMO cron persistence relaunching binary every 15 minutes Installation High
Hunts cron entries (crontab edits, files dropped into /etc/cron.*, /var/spool/cron/) that schedule a binary from /tmp, /var/tmp, or /dev/shm on a 15-minute cadence — the exact relaunch pattern Fortinet documented for C0XMO. Rationale: Article explicitly says cron jobs relaunch the binary every 15 minutes. Filtering writes to canonical Linux cron paths while excluding package managers (the only legitimate writers in most fleets) keeps signal high.
ATT&CKT1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let CronPaths = dynamic(["/var/spool/cron/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/crontab","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.weekly/","/etc/cron.monthly/"]);
let TmpPaths = dynamic(["/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (CronPaths)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "crontab" or InitiatingProcessFileName has "crontab"
) on DeviceId
| where FolderPath has_any (CronPaths)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let CronPaths = dynamic(["/var/spool/cron/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/crontab","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.weekly/","/etc/cron.monthly/"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CronPaths)
| extend SuspiciousBody = TargetFilePath
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C0XMO Python scanner module install (paramiko + beautifulsoup4) Installation Medium
Hunts the very specific pip install footprint Fortinet describes for the C0XMO scanner: a Python script that installs `requests`, `paramiko`, and `beautifulsoup4` together before launching worker-thread SSH/Telnet scanning. The combination on a server that wasn't doing Python ML/web scraping yesterday is a strong signal. Rationale: Article names the exact packages: `requests`, `paramiko`, `beautifulsoup4`. The `paramiko + beautifulsoup4` pair specifically is unusual outside scraping-with-SSH workloads; combined with `install` in the cmdline it's a clean fingerprint of the scanner-bootstrap step.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("paramiko","beautifulsoup4") and ProcessCommandLine has "install"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_all ("paramiko","requests","install")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3") or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("paramiko","beautifulsoup4")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_all ("paramiko","beautifulsoup4")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C0XMO rival botnet and red-team process termination spree Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the C0XMO defense-evasion phase: actively scanning running processes for competitor botnets / red-team tooling / programming/network services and killing them. A short-burst of `kill -9` / `pkill` / `killall` against a list of well-known botnet binary names is the signature. Rationale: Article calls out the rival-killing behaviour explicitly. Threshold (≥3 distinct rival tokens killed in 2 min by the same host/user) catches the burst-kill pattern while one-off `pkill xmrig` from a sysadmin doesn't trip.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1489
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let RivalTokens = dynamic(["mirai","gafgyt","tsunami","mozi","hajime","lucifer","moobot","satori","xmrig","kinsing","sliver","meterpreter","chisel","frp","merlin"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("kill","pkill","killall")
| extend MatchedRivals = set_intersect(RivalTokens, extract_all(@"(?i)([a-z0-9_-]+)", tostring(ProcessCommandLine)))
| where array_length(MatchedRivals) >= 3
| summarize KillCount = count(), Rivals = make_set(MatchedRivals,50), AnyCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), AnyParent = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 2m)
| where KillCount >= 3
| order by Timestamp desc
let RivalTokens = dynamic(["mirai","gafgyt","tsunami","mozi","hajime","lucifer","moobot","satori","xmrig","kinsing","sliver","meterpreter","chisel","frp","merlin"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("kill","pkill","killall") or TargetProcessName has_any ("kill","pkill","killall")
| extend Cmd = coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| extend MatchedRivals = set_intersect(RivalTokens, extract_all(@"(?i)([a-z0-9_-]+)", tostring(Cmd)))
| where array_length(MatchedRivals) >= 3
| summarize KillCount = count(), Rivals = make_set(MatchedRivals,50), AnyCmd = any(Cmd), AnyParent = any(ParentProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m)
| where KillCount >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*\/kill OR *\/pkill OR *\/killall) @process.command_line:(*mirai* OR *gafgyt* OR *tsunami* OR *mozi* OR *hajime* OR *xmrig* OR *kinsing* OR *sliver* OR *meterpreter* OR *moobot*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/(pkill|killall|kill)$/i
| regex("(?i)(mirai|gafgyt|tsunami|mozi|hajime|lucifer|moobot|satori|xmrig|kinsing|sliver|meterpreter|chisel|frp|merlin)", field=CommandLine)

| KillEvents >= 3
ENDPOINT

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

logsource:

detection:

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Access to law-firm-impersonating IT helpdesk phishing domain · [LLM] Privnote.com access on endpoint hosting an active remote-support session · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Unsanctioned RMM tool install or first execution (AnyDesk/Zoho/Bomgar/SuperOps) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to known Silent Ransom Group C2 / leak-site infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Access to law-firm-impersonating IT helpdesk phishing domain Delivery High
Hunts DNS/web traffic to domains matching the Silent Ransom Group naming pattern `<org>-itdesk[.]com`, `<org>-it[.]com`, `<org>-helpdesk[.]com` used to lend credibility to callback-phishing IT impersonation calls. These domains are throwaways spun up per-victim; any hit warrants immediate triage of the contacted user. Rationale: Mandiant's report explicitly calls out three naming patterns `<org>-itdesk[.]com`, `<org>-it[.]com`, `<org>-helpdesk[.]com`. The regex anchors on the literal `-(it|itdesk|helpdesk).com` suffix and excludes a known-vendor allowlist to keep FP rate low. Cross-checked with FBI FLASH advisory referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ic3.gov/CSA-Notice/2025 • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1032/
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let SuspectPattern = dynamic(["-itdesk.com","-helpdesk.com","-it.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SuspectPattern)
| extend Host = tolower(RemoteUrl)
| where Host matches regex @"^[a-z0-9-]{3,}-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com(:\d+)?(/.*)?$"
| where not(Host matches regex @"^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce|atlassian|zoom|slack|github)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectPattern = dynamic(["-itdesk.com","-helpdesk.com","-it.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (SuspectPattern)
| extend Host = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where Host matches regex @"^[a-z0-9-]{3,}-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$"
| where not(Host matches regex @"^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce|atlassian|zoom|slack|github)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Silent Ransom Group IT-Impersonating Phishing Domain Resolution
id: 9b8c1d5e-a432-4e1c-bb40-3a2e9b6a7f01
description: Detects DNS queries to domains matching UNC3753/Luna Moth callback-phishing IT-helpdesk impersonation naming pattern (-itdesk.com / -it.com / -helpdesk.com).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/silent-ransom-group-targets-law-firms-with-fake-it-support-calls/
  - https://www.ic3.gov/CSA-Notice/2025
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/07
tags:
  - attack.t1566.004
  - attack.t1583.001
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: dns
selection:
  QueryName|re: '^[a-z0-9-]{3,}-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$'
filter_vendor:
  QueryName|re: '^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce|atlassian|zoom|slack|github)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$'
condition: selection and not filter_vendor
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR cloudtrail) (@DnsQuery:(*-itdesk.com OR *-helpdesk.com OR *-it.com) OR @QueryName:(*-itdesk.com OR *-helpdesk.com OR *-it.com) OR @network.destination.domain:(*-itdesk.com OR *-helpdesk.com OR *-it.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/^[a-z0-9-]{3,}-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$/i
| NOT DomainName=/^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce|atlassian|zoom|slack|github)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query="*-itdesk.com" OR DNS.query="*-it.com" OR DNS.query="*-helpdesk.com" by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | where NOT match(query, "^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query="*-itdesk.com" OR DNS.query="*-it.com" OR DNS.query="*-helpdesk.com" by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | where NOT match(query, "^(microsoft|apple|google|amazon|adobe|cisco|salesforce)-(it|itdesk|helpdesk)\.com$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Privnote.com access on endpoint hosting an active remote-support session Delivery High
Hunts for browser navigation to privnote[.]com (self-destructing-note service) from hosts where Quick Assist, Microsoft Terminal Services, or unsanctioned remote-support tooling is concurrently active. Mandiant specifically calls out privnote[.]com as the channel UNC3753 uses to push installer URLs and commands to victims during the IT-impersonation call. Rationale: Mandiant: 'threat actors also use privnote[.]com ... to share installation links and commands with targets during remote support sessions.' Pairing privnote access with a remote-support tool in a 60-minute window converts a low-fidelity domain hit into a high-fidelity TTP match. RemoteIP/RemoteUrl confirmed only on DeviceNetworkEvents per schema. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1566
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
let PrivnoteHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "privnote.com"
  | project PrivnoteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, User = InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Browser = InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl;
let RemoteSupport = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName in~ ("quickassist.exe","mstsc.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe","AnyDesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe")
     or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("quickassist.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe")
     or FileName has_any ("bomgar","beyondtrust","superops")
  | project RmmTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, RmmProc = FileName, RmmCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
PrivnoteHits
| join kind=inner RemoteSupport on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', PrivnoteTime, RmmTime)) <= 60
| project PrivnoteTime, RmmTime, DeviceName, User, Browser, RemoteUrl, RmmProc, RmmCmd
| order by PrivnoteTime desc
let PrivnoteHits = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has "privnote.com"
  | project PrivnoteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url;
let RemoteSupport = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("quickassist.exe","mstsc.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe","bomgar","beyondtrust","superops")
     or TargetProcessName has_any ("quickassist.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe","bomgar","superops")
  | project RmmTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RmmProc = TargetProcessName, RmmCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine;
PrivnoteHits
| join kind=inner RemoteSupport on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', PrivnoteTime, RmmTime)) <= 60
| project PrivnoteTime, RmmTime, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, RmmProc, RmmCmd
| order by PrivnoteTime desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@network.destination.domain:privnote.com OR @DnsQuery:privnote.com OR @url:*privnote.com*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/privnote\.com$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(quickassist|mstsc|anydesk|zohoassist|bomgar|beyondtrust|superops)/i}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ImageFileName], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*privnote.com*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=inner src [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("quickassist.exe","mstsc.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe","bomgar*.exe","superops*.exe") by Processes.dest | rename Processes.dest as src | fields src] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*privnote.com*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("quickassist.exe","mstsc.exe","anydesk.exe","zohoassist.exe","bomgar*.exe","superops*.exe") by Processes.dest | rename Processes.dest as src | fields src] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Unsanctioned RMM tool install or first execution (AnyDesk/Zoho/Bomgar/SuperOps) Installation High
Detects first-time-on-host execution or fresh installation of AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, BeyondTrust Bomgar, or SuperOps — the four RMM tools Mandiant calls out as UNC3753's initial-access toolset on victim endpoints. Anti-joined to a 30-day per-host baseline so legitimate IT-sanctioned RMMs don't fire. Rationale: Mandiant explicitly names AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, and SuperOps as the RMM tools UNC3753 pushes during the IT-impersonation remote-support session. The 30-day per-host baseline + user-path filter cuts the noise that would otherwise come from IT-sanctioned AnyDesk/Bomgar deployments running from Program Files. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/ • https://www.ic3.gov/CSA-Notice/2025
ATT&CKT1219 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let Baseline = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(7d))
  | where FileName has_any ("AnyDesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","Bomgar","BeyondTrust","SuperOps")
  | summarize by DeviceId, FileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName has_any ("AnyDesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","Bomgar","BeyondTrust","SuperOps")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on DeviceId, FileName
| extend SuspiciousFolder = FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\",@"\AppData\",@"\Temp\",@"\Downloads\",@"\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SuspiciousFolder
| order by Timestamp desc
let Baseline = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(7d))
  | where TargetProcessName has_any ("AnyDesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","Bomgar","BeyondTrust","SuperOps")
  | summarize by DvcHostname, TargetProcessName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("AnyDesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","Bomgar","BeyondTrust","SuperOps")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on DvcHostname, TargetProcessName
| extend SuspiciousFolder = TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Users\",@"\AppData\",@"\Temp\",@"\Downloads\",@"\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SuspiciousFolder
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: First-Seen RMM Tool Execution Linked to Silent Ransom Group
id: 7f1d9824-3b21-4a5d-9c4e-6e2f1a8d2c33
description: Detects first-time-on-host execution of AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, BeyondTrust Bomgar, or SuperOps — RMM tools Mandiant attributes to UNC3753/Luna Moth for law-firm initial access.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/silent-ransom-group-targets-law-firms-with-fake-it-support-calls/
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/07
tags:

  product: windows
selection_img:
  Image|endswith:
    - '\AnyDesk.exe'
    - '\ZohoAssist.exe'
    - '\BomgarPac.exe'

    - '\SuperOps.exe'
    - '\SuperOpsRMM.exe'

    - '\Users\'
    - '\AppData\'
    - '\Temp\'

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) @Image:(*\\AnyDesk.exe OR *\\anydesk.exe OR *\\ZohoAssist.exe OR *\\zohoassist.exe OR *\\Bomgar* OR *\\BeyondTrust* OR *\\SuperOps*) (@Image:(*\\Users\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\Public\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(AnyDesk|ZohoAssist|Bomgar|BeyondTrust|SuperOps)[A-Za-z0-9_]*\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(Users|AppData|Temp|Downloads|Public)\\/i

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","anydesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","zohoassist.exe","BomgarPac*.exe","BeyondTrustRA*.exe","SuperOps*.exe","SuperOpsRMM*.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eventstats min(firstTime) as baselineFirst by dest process_name | where firstTime = baselineFirst AND firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","anydesk.exe","ZohoAssist.exe","zohoassist.exe","BomgarPac*.exe","BeyondTrustRA*.exe","SuperOps*.exe","SuperOpsRMM*.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eventstats min(firstTime) as baselineFirst by dest process_name | where firstTime = baselineFirst AND firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d")
[LLM] Rclone or WinSCP exfiltration to non-corporate external destination exfiltration High
Hunts WinSCP or Rclone executions making outbound connections to non-corporate destinations — the canonical UNC3753 data-theft pattern after the RMM session. Pairs the process-creation event with the network egress to surface only invocations that actually moved data off-prem. Rationale: Mandiant: 'exfiltrating the data using tools such as WinSCP or Rclone.' Joining process create to outbound network on the same DeviceId+ProcessId within 30 minutes converts a noisy process detection into a high-fidelity exfil signal. KnownCorpDest exclusion suppresses sanctioned SharePoint/OneDrive sync traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1040/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567.002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1048
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let RcloneProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName in~ ("rclone.exe","winscp.exe","winscp.com")
  | where AccountName !endswith "$"
  | project ProcTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, FolderPath;
let ExfilNet = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("rclone.exe","winscp.exe","winscp.com")
  | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
  | where RemotePort in (21, 22, 80, 443, 8080, 8443)
  | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ProcessId = InitiatingProcessId, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort;
RcloneProcs
| join kind=inner ExfilNet on DeviceId, ProcessId
| where NetTime between (ProcTime .. ProcTime + 30m)
| extend KnownCorpDest = RemoteUrl has_any ("sharepoint.com","onedrive.com","office.com","box.com","dropboxapi.com")
| where not(KnownCorpDest)
| project ProcTime, NetTime, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by ProcTime desc
let RcloneProcs = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetProcessName has_any ("rclone.exe","winscp.exe","winscp.com")
  | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
  | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessId;
let ExfilNet = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DvcAction != "Deny"
  | where DstPortNumber in (21, 22, 80, 443, 8080, 8443)
  | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes;
RcloneProcs
| join kind=inner ExfilNet on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (ProcTime .. ProcTime + 30m)

[LLM] Outbound connection to known Silent Ransom Group C2 / leak-site infrastructure Command & Control High
Alerts on any outbound traffic from a corporate endpoint to the IPs and domains attributed by Mandiant + Resecurity to UNC3753/Luna Moth fast-flux infrastructure and the business-data-leaks[.]com leak portal. Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.

   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")

          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")

| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

BleepingComputer
2026-06-06 6 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound traffic from CVE-2026-3300 mass-exploitation source IPs to web servers
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2026-3300 Everest Forms Pro eval() payload in HTTP request to Complex Calculation form
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WordPress 'diksimarina' rogue administrator account activity in web/access logs · [LLM] PHP webshell drop in WordPress wp-content directories by web-server process
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] CVE-2026-3300 Everest Forms Pro eval() payload in HTTP request to Complex Calculation form Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests that carry the literal exploit signature of the Everest Forms Pro Complex Calculation eval() injection: a form-field value starting with a single quote followed by wp_insert_user() and a // PHP comment marker, often with the rogue username 'diksimarina'. Targets the unauthenticated RCE on Everest Forms Pro <=1.9.12 directly at the WAF/web-log layer. Rationale: Uses three article-specific strings: the literal username 'diksimarina' (confirmed by Wordfence and corroborated by The Hacker News and Infosecurity Magazine), the wp_insert_user() PHP function from the injected payload, and the Everest Forms calculation endpoint path. These three tokens combined make HTTP body/query matches very high fidelity. Cross-checked against Wordfence advisory and GHSA-jfqc-5rvh-wp99. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/06/attackers-actively-exploiting-critical-vulnerability-in-everest-forms-pro-plugin/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-exploit-critical-everest-forms.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jfqc-5rvh-wp99
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| where RemoteIP in ("202.56.2.126","209.146.60.26","15.235.166.18","185.78.165.153")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("everest-forms","everest_forms_calculation")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let exploit_ips = dynamic(["202.56.2.126","209.146.60.26","15.235.166.18","185.78.165.153"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "POST"
   | where csUriStem has_any ("/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php","/?everest_forms_ajax","everest-forms") or csUriQuery has_any ("everest_forms","complex_calculation","wp_insert_user","diksimarina")

[LLM] Inbound traffic from CVE-2026-3300 mass-exploitation source IPs to web servers Delivery High
Alerts on any network connection or web request originating from the four IPs Wordfence attributes to the active CVE-2026-3300 exploitation campaign (202.56.2.126, 209.146.60.26, 15.235.166.18, 185.78.165.153). These IPs have driven 29,300+ exploit attempts since 2026-04-13; any successful TCP/HTTP session from them to an internal WordPress host warrants triage. Rationale: Four IPs are explicitly attributed by Wordfence as the primary CVE-2026-3300 exploitation sources (Wordfence flagged 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26 as 'primary' originators). Two additional IPs come from the pre-extracted IOC bundle. Detection is high-fidelity because these IPs are attacker-owned infra with no legitimate business reason to reach internal web servers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/06/attackers-actively-exploiting-critical-vulnerability-in-everest-forms-pro-plugin/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-everest-forms-pro-flaw-exploited-to-take-over-wordpress-sites/

| summarize ConnectionCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Ports=make_set(LocalPort) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| extend Campaign="CVE-2026-3300"
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] WordPress 'diksimarina' rogue administrator account activity in web/access logs Installation High
Hunts any HTTP request, log line, or audit entry that references the literal username 'diksimarina' — the rogue WordPress administrator account created by the CVE-2026-3300 wp_insert_user() payload. Per the Wordfence advisory the account also uses the email diksimarina@gmail.com. Catches both the creation request and any subsequent attacker login or wp-admin activity tied to the account. Rationale: The username 'diksimarina' is the single most distinctive IOC in the article — the BleepingComputer body explicitly says administrators should 'review log files and administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina.' Wordfence corroborates and adds the email diksimarina@gmail.com. Any production log mention of this string is a strong indicator of a successful CVE-2026-3300 exploit on that host. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/06/attackers-actively-exploiting-critical-vulnerability-in-everest-forms-pro-plugin/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-exploit-critical-everest-forms.html • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/everest-forms-pro-rce-actively/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.001 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RemoteUrl has "diksimarina" or RemoteUrl has "diksimarina%40gmail.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort, ActionType
| union (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName has "diksimarina" or FolderPath has "diksimarina" or AdditionalFields has "diksimarina"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 60d;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
   | where csUriStem has "diksimarina" or csUriQuery has "diksimarina" or csReferer has "diksimarina" or csUserName =~ "diksimarina"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, src=cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserName, scStatus, csUserAgent),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
   | where CsUriStem has "diksimarina" or CsUriQuery has "diksimarina" or Referer has "diksimarina"
   | project TimeGenerated, src=CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, ScStatus, UserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
   | where RequestURL has "diksimarina" or Message has "diksimarina" or SourceUserName =~ "diksimarina" or DestinationHostName =~ "diksimarina"
   | project TimeGenerated, DeviceProduct, src=SourceIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Message),
  (Syslog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
   | where SyslogMessage has "diksimarina"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Facility, SyslogMessage)
| extend ioc="diksimarina", cve="CVE-2026-3300"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHP webshell drop in WordPress wp-content directories by web-server process Installation Medium
Hunts file writes of .php files into wp-content/uploads, wp-content/themes, or wp-content/plugins by IIS/Apache/Nginx/php-fpm worker processes. This is the canonical post-exploitation behaviour the article warns about following diksimarina admin compromise: the attacker uploads webshells or backdoors via the WordPress plugin/theme uploader once admin access is established. Rationale: Article explicitly lists 'planting backdoors and webshells' as the post-compromise impact and notes wp-content/uploads as the typical drop directory implied by 'modifying content, installing plugins and themes'. Pivot is articulated through three high-fidelity constraints: web-server-process parent (w3wp/php-fpm/httpd), WordPress plugin/theme/upload path, and PHP-executable extension — combined this is rarely benign outside of admin-driven plugin installs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/06/attackers-actively-exploiting-critical-vulnerability-in-everest-forms-pro-plugin/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-everest-forms-pro-flaw-exploited-to-take-over-wordpress-sites/

| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".php7"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc

| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/wp-content/uploads/","\\wp-content\\uploads\\","/wp-content/plugins/","\\wp-content\\plugins\\","/wp-content/themes/","\\wp-content\\themes\\")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","php7","phps")

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Miasma Worm Hits Microsoft Again: Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents

StepSecurity
2026-06-06 12 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On June 5, 2026, the Miasma worm campaign reached Microsoft's Azure GitHub organizations. GitHub disabled 73 repositories across four Microsoft GitHub organizations after a malicious commit was pushed to the Azure/durabletask repository using a previously compromised contributor account. The attack planted configuration files that execute a credential-harvesting payload when a developer opens the repository in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Suspicious commit pattern: '[skip ci]' with backdated timestamp adding only IDE config files · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] node.exe spawned by Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini executing .github/setup.js · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma Worm Hits Microsoft Again: Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositori
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious AI coding-agent hook configs written to repo (.claude/.gemini/.cursor/.vscode)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound DNS / HTTP to Miasma C2 (git-service.com / m-kosche.com) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Malicious AI coding-agent hook configs written to repo (.claude/.gemini/.cursor/.vscode) Installation High
Hunts the Miasma worm's signature artifact: simultaneous creation of SessionStart hooks and folderOpen tasks in .claude/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, and .vscode/tasks.json — all pointing at node .github/setup.js. This is the precise file-set planted in the June 5 2026 Azure/durabletask commit 5f456b8. Rationale: The five planted-file paths are verbatim from the article's 'Five Planted Files, Four Attack Vectors' section. Requiring >=2 co-occurrence per host suppresses single legitimate .vscode/tasks.json edits while keeping near-zero FP on the Miasma file-set. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://github.com/step-security/supply-chain-firewall
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
| extend Artifact = case(
    FolderPath has @"\.claude\settings.json", "claude-hook",
    FolderPath has @"\.gemini\settings.json", "gemini-hook",
    FolderPath has @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", "cursor-prompt-injection",
    FolderPath has @"\.vscode\tasks.json", "vscode-folderopen",
    FolderPath has @"\.github\setup.js", "miasma-payload", "other")
| summarize ArtifactsSeen = make_set(Artifact), Paths = make_set(FolderPath), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where array_length(ArtifactsSeen) >= 2  // co-occurrence of >=2 of the 5 planted files
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
| extend Artifact = case(
    TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\settings.json", "claude-hook",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.gemini\settings.json", "gemini-hook",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", "cursor-prompt-injection",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\tasks.json", "vscode-folderopen",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.github\setup.js", "miasma-payload", "other")
| summarize ArtifactsSeen = make_set(Artifact), Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where array_length(ArtifactsSeen) >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Miasma Worm AI-Agent Hook Config Planted
id: 8a2a4e0f-3d9c-4b7d-9b4f-1d2e7c61a210
description: Detects creation of SessionStart hooks / folderOpen tasks / Cursor prompt-injection rules that the Miasma worm plants in compromised repos to auto-execute node .github/setup.js when a developer opens the project in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code.
references:

| _count >= 2

[LLM] node.exe spawned by Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini executing .github/setup.js Exploitation High
Hunts the Miasma worm's automatic execution chain: VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI launching node.exe with .github/setup.js as the script argument. This is the runtime detonation produced when a developer simply opens a repo containing the planted hook configs. Rationale: Article quotes the exact command 'node .github/setup.js' invoked by all four planted configs (Claude SessionStart, Gemini SessionStart, Cursor prompt injection, VS Code folderOpen task). Anchoring on parent IDE + node.exe + setup.js path is high-fidelity because legitimate projects rarely store bootstrap scripts under .github/. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/ • https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/tasks#_run-behavior
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1204.002

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@".github\setup.js", ".github/setup.js")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@".github\setup.js", ".github/setup.js")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm node.exe Auto-Executing .github/setup.js From IDE
id: 7e5f1a0d-9b2c-4a18-9e2d-2c4f3a7b8e02
description: Detects node.exe spawned by VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI with .github/setup.js on the command line — the Miasma worm's auto-execution on folder open.
references:

logsource:

detection:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2

| CommandLine=/\.github[\\\/]setup\.js/i

[LLM] Outbound DNS / HTTP to Miasma C2 (git-service.com / m-kosche.com) Command & Control High
Hunts resolution or connection to the Miasma worm's credential-exfiltration infrastructure: check.git-service.com, git-service.com, and t.m-kosche.com. These domains receive harvested AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/dev-tool secrets from the planted payload. Rationale: Three domains are explicitly listed in the article's pre-extracted IOCs (check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, git-service.com). Article says credential-harvesting payload exfiltrates AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/dev-tool secrets, so DNS+network egress to these domains is high-fidelity C2. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-worm-hits-microsoft-again-azure-functions-action-and-72-other-repositories-disabled-after-supply-chain-attack-targeting-ai-coding-agents
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com") or RemoteUrl in~ ("check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where Name has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryType = QueryTypeName, Result),
  (ImDnsActivity
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DnsQuery has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryType = DnsQueryTypeName, Result = DnsResponseCodeName),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com") or RequestURL has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), QueryType = "proxy", Result = DeviceAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Suspicious commit pattern: '[skip ci]' with backdated timestamp adding only IDE config files Delivery Medium
Hunts the Miasma commit fingerprint: a single push where 5 files added / 0 source files modified, commit message ends with '[skip ci]', author date backdated to a pre-2024 timestamp, and the added paths include AI-agent config dirs. Detects via GitHub Audit Log shipped to Sentinel/Defender via CloudAppEvents or to Datadog via the GitHub integration. Rationale: Article details the exact commit fingerprint: commit 5f456b8 with message 'Switched DataConverter to OrchestrationContext [skip ci]', 5 files added / 0 source files modified, backdated to 2020-03-09T15:59:47Z (six years before push). The conjunction of [skip ci] + backdated author date + added IDE-config paths is the Miasma operator signature. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application == "GitHub"
| where ActionType in ("Repositories.Push","RepositoriesPush","git.push")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has "[skip ci]"
| where Raw has_any (".claude/settings.json",".gemini/settings.json",".cursor/rules/setup.mdc",".vscode/tasks.json",".github/setup.js")
| extend AuthorDate = extract(@"author[^\d]+(\d{4})-\d{2}-\d{2}", 1, Raw)
| where isnotempty(AuthorDate) and toint(AuthorDate) < 2024
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, ObjectName, AuthorDate, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires GitHub Audit Log connector (GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL) or CommonSecurityLog ingest
GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where action_s == "git.push" or action_s == "repo.push"
| where commits_s has "[skip ci]"
| where commits_s has_any (".claude/settings.json",".gemini/settings.json",".cursor/rules/setup.mdc",".vscode/tasks.json",".github/setup.js")
| extend AuthorYear = extract(@"author[^\d]+(\d{4})-\d{2}-\d{2}", 1, commits_s)
| where isnotempty(AuthorYear) and toint(AuthorYear) < 2024
| project TimeGenerated, actor_s, actor_ip_s, repo_s, commits_s, AuthorYear
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @evt.name:git.push @commits.message:*"[skip ci]"* (@commits.added:(*.claude/settings.json* OR *.gemini/settings.json* OR *.cursor/rules/setup.mdc* OR *.vscode/tasks.json* OR *.github/setup.js*))
CLOUD
`github_audit` action=git.push | spath input=raw_event | search commits{}.message="*[skip ci]*" (commits{}.added{}="*.claude/settings.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.gemini/settings.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.cursor/rules/setup.mdc" OR commits{}.added{}="*.vscode/tasks.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.github/setup.js") | eval author_year=substr('commits{}.timestamp',1,4) | where author_year<"2024" | table _time repo actor commits{}.id commits{}.message commits{}.added{} author_year
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
