Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack

StepSecurity
2026-06-06 14 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] rope.pyz dropper executed as /tmp/managed.pyz from durabletask import · [LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence written under ~/.config/systemd/user/ · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to TeamPCP rope.pyz C2 infrastructure (check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com / 160.119.64.3) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. [LLM] Pip install of compromised Microsoft durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 Delivery High
Hunts for pip / python invocations that explicitly request or have resolved to the three trojanized durabletask versions published to PyPI on 19 May 2026. Targets Linux CI runners, build agents, and cloud workloads where the package would be picked up. Rationale: Anchored on the three article-confirmed malicious versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) and the publication window of 19 May 2026 16:19 UTC onward. Process telemetry of explicit `pip install durabletask==X.Y.Z` invocations is high-fidelity since the legitimate prior version is 1.4.0 (Apr 8). Tier=alerting because of specific version pins. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask<1.4.1" and Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))

[LLM] rope.pyz dropper executed as /tmp/managed.pyz from durabletask import Installation High
Hunts the unique payload-execution fingerprint from the TeamPCP supply chain attack: a python3 process whose command line references /tmp/managed.pyz, typically spawned via start_new_session=True from a parent python3 -c "import durabletask". Highest-fidelity single signal in the campaign. Rationale: /tmp/managed.pyz is the article-confirmed payload filename the dropper writes via urllib.request.urlretrieve and immediately executes with subprocess.Popen(["python3", "/tmp/managed.pyz"]). The string is unique to this campaign — virtually zero benign use of that exact path. Parent-process pivot on `python3 -c "import durabletask"` adds the chain-of-custody. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1204.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and FileName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp asc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (ParentProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated asc

Detects DNS lookups or outbound network connections to the article-confirmed C2 domains used to fetch the rope.pyz dropper and to identify the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Single-hit alerting; these IOCs have no legitimate use. Rationale: Three article-confirmed IOCs with no legitimate use: check.git-service.com (hosts rope.pyz), t.m-kosche.com (secondary attribution beacon tying to TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud), and resolving IP 160.119.64.3 (HostUS / AS7489, AFRINIC). Domain `git-service.com` was registered via NameSilo 16 May 2026 — only 3 days before the attack — so trailing-day FPs are vanishingly unlikely. No external sources cross-checked.

[LLM] gh auth token / gpg-decrypt credential harvesting by python3 child Actions on Objectives High
Detects the rope.pyz collector pattern of harvesting GitHub Personal Access Tokens via gh CLI and GPG-protected secrets via `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`, parented by a python3 process — exactly the cmdline strings the article ties to managed.pyz parallel collectors. Rationale: Article-verbatim cmdline strings: `gh auth token`, `gh auth status --show-token`, and `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`. The literal passphrase `anon` is an attacker-chosen string with no legitimate use — humans do not use that passphrase for real GPG-protected material. Parented by python3 narrows out interactive developer use of gh. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1555 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (FileName =~ "gh" and (ProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (FileName =~ "gpg" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
         by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where CommandCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (ActingProcessName =~ "gh" and (ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (ActingProcessName =~ "gpg" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
         by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessId, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence written under ~/.config/systemd/user/ Installation High
Detects creation of the article-named `pgsql-monitor.service` user-level systemd unit file, and the follow-up `systemctl --user daemon-reload` spawned by a python3 process — the exact persistence mechanism each of the four managed.pyz collector instances installs. Rationale: Article names the exact persistence artefact (`pgsql-monitor.service`) and the exact cmdline (`systemctl --user daemon-reload`) spawned by each of the four parallel managed.pyz instances. User-level systemd persistence under `~/.config/systemd/user/` is rare on CI runners and cloud-workload base images. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let file_persist = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName endswith ".service")
     or FileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName="systemctl", FolderPath=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by Timestamp desc
let file_persist = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user" and TargetFileName endswith ".service")
     or TargetFileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName="systemctl", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ParentProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP pgsql-monitor.service Systemd Persistence (durabletask Compromise)
id: 4c2e9f73-86a1-4b2d-b3f8-9e7a4d1c8b25
description: Detects creation of the pgsql-monitor.service user-level systemd unit that rope.pyz installs for persistence, or python3-parented systemctl --user daemon-reload invocations that activate it.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1543.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_named:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '/pgsql-monitor.service'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/.config/systemd/user/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.service'
  condition: selection_named or selection_path
level: high
(source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:(*/.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor.service OR */.config/systemd/user/*.service)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(python OR python3) @process.command_line:*"systemctl --user daemon-reload"*)
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten AND (regex("/\\.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor\\.service$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.config/systemd/user/.*\\.service$", field=TargetFileName))) OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 AND ImageFileName=/\/systemctl$/i AND regex("--user.*daemon-reload", field=CommandLine) AND ParentBaseFileName=/python3?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
(`tstats` summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="pgsql-monitor.service" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="systemctl" AND Processes.process="*--user*daemon-reload*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="python3" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
(`tstats` summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="pgsql-monitor.service" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="systemctl" AND Processes.process="*--user*daemon-reload*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="python3" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Burst of AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession from stolen durabletask credentials Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the article's lateral-movement pattern: stolen ~/.aws/credentials being used to enumerate SSM-managed instances and run remote commands or shell sessions. Looks for a single IAM principal calling DescribeInstanceInformation followed by SendCommand or StartSession from a fresh source IP within a short window. Rationale: Article confirms `propagates to other machines through AWS SSM and Kubernetes kubectl exec` after harvesting AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials. The high-signal pattern is DescribeInstanceInformation immediately followed by SendCommand or StartSession from the same principal within a short window — classic SSM-as-RCE TTP. Hunting tier because legitimate ops engineers do this too. Defender / Sentinel KQL left empty because their canonical schemas in this tenant do not include AWSCloudTrail; the Sentinel column list above contains no AWSCloudTrail table — operators ingesting CloudTrail via the AWS S3 connector would have a `AWSCloudTrail` table not in the canonical schema. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1078.004 T1580
Data sourcesAuthentication
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(DescribeInstanceInformation OR SendCommand OR StartSession OR ResumeSession) @evt.outcome:success @userIdentity.type:(IAMUser OR AssumedRole)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, awsRegion, requestParameters.instanceIds, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["DescribeInstanceInformation", "SendCommand", "StartSession", "ResumeSession", "GetCommandInvocation"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
| stats count(*) as calls, count_distinct(eventName) as event_types, count_distinct(sourceIPAddress) as src_ips, earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen, latest(@timestamp) as last_seen by userIdentity.arn
| filter event_types >= 2
| sort last_seen desc
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` (eventName=DescribeInstanceInformation OR eventName=SendCommand OR eventName=StartSession OR eventName=ResumeSession) errorCode="*" OR errorCode=NULL
| eval principal=coalesce('userIdentity.arn','userIdentity.userName')
| stats earliest(_time) as firstSeen latest(_time) as lastSeen dc(eventName) as eventTypes values(eventName) as events values(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPs dc(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPCount count by principal
| where eventTypes >= 2 AND srcIPCount >= 1
| eval windowSec=lastSeen-firstSeen
| where windowSec <= 1800
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - firstSeen
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("__init__.py", "task.py", "roulette.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/managed.pyz", "/dev/null", "/etc/timezone", "/usr/bin/pgmonitor.py") or FileName in~ ("__init__.py", "task.py", "roulette.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
